source_text: Hoc ergo nunc sibi proposuit, et praemittit interrogationem meam. Dicis ergo, inquit, ideo illos esse sub diabolo, quia de sexus utriusque commixtione nascuntur? Ad quod qualem satisfactionem referat, audiamus. Dico, inquit, plane propter delictum illos esse sub diabolo; ideo autem expertes non esse delicti, quia de illa commixtione sunt nati, quae sine pudenda libidine non potest etiam quod honestum est operari. Dixit hoc etiam beatissimae memoriae Ambrosius [n159] . O calamitosam hominis pravitatem! O intentionem nefandam! O falsitatem erubescendam!
pass_a_gloss: This therefore he now proposed to himself, and he sends ahead my interrogation. You say therefore, he says, that they are therefore under the devil, because they are born from the mingling of each sex? To which of what sort a satisfaction he reports, let us hear. I say, he says, plainly that they are under the devil on account of offense; but that they are therefore not without share of offense, because they were born from that mingling which cannot work even what is honorable without shameful lust. Blessed Ambrose of most blessed memory said this also. O calamitous crookedness of a human! O nefarious intention! O falsehood to be blushed at!

lemmas.lexica: LS libido; Blaise pudenda libido vs nuptiae
LS opus; Blaise God's works vs devil's

pass_b_english: He now puts this before himself, beginning with my question: “So you say,” he writes, “that they are under the devil because they are born from the union of the two sexes?” Let us hear what explanation he gives. “I certainly say,” he replies, “that they are under the devil because of an offense. They are not free of the offense because they were born from that union which cannot perform even what is honorable without shameful lust. Ambrose, of most blessed memory, also said this” (Augustine, On Marriage and Concupiscence 2.5.15). What disastrous perversity in the man! What an unspeakable intention! What shameful falsehood!

choices.why: Julian's pudenda libido is the appetite accompanying union, not a created substance of sin.
Julian defends marital union (commixtio) as God's work, not the devil's property.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)
